1. **Creating PRs**: Always check for uncommitted changes first with `git status`
3. **Use `--output`**: For machine-readable output, use `-o json` or `-o yaml`

content.user_title: Manage Gitea Workflows with tea CLI
content.value_statement: Gitea work often requires precise tea CLI commands across pull requests, issues, and repositories. This skill provides concise command guidance for common Gitea tasks.
actual_capabilities: Detects likely Gitea repositories by checking git remote hosts.
Guides authentication checks with the tea login list command.
Provides tea commands for creating, listing, viewing, checking out, and merging pull requests.
Provides tea commands for creating, listing, viewing, closing, and commenting on issues.
Provides tea commands for repository clone and fork operations.
Recommends JSON or YAML output flags for machine-readable tea results.
limitations: Requires the tea CLI to be installed and configured by the user.
Requires access to the target Gitea instance and repository permissions.
Does not replace Gitea authorization, branch protection, or review policies.
Provides command guidance only; command results depend on the local environment.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Check repository state, verify Gitea context, and create a pull request with tea commands.

use_cases.title: Triage Repository Issues
use_cases.description: List open issues, view details, add comments, and close resolved work through tea.

use_cases.title: Collect Structured Gitea Data
use_cases.description: Use JSON or YAML output from tea to inspect pull requests and issues in automation.

prompt_templates.title: Check Gitea Context
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether this repository appears to use Gitea, then show the tea authentication command I should run.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Pull Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me prepare a Gitea pull request. Check for uncommitted changes first, then give me the tea command with a clear title and description.

prompt_templates.title: Review Issue Status
prompt_templates.prompt: List the open Gitea issues, show how to inspect one issue, and provide the command to add a short comment.

prompt_templates.title: Produce Automation-Friendly Output
prompt_templates.prompt: Give me tea commands that return pull request and issue data in JSON, then explain which command I should run for CI inspection.

output_examples.input: I need to open a pull request on our Gitea repository.
output_examples.output: The skill asks you to check git status, confirms tea authentication, and provides a pull request creation command with title and description fields.

output_examples.input: Show me open issues in a format that another tool can read.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends the tea issue list command with structured output enabled, then explains how to view a selected issue.

output_examples.input: I want to inspect pull requests before triggering CI work.
output_examples.output: The skill points to pull request listing and viewing commands, then recommends structured output for reliable automation decisions.

best_practices: Verify the git remote host before assuming a repository uses Gitea.
Check tea authentication before running repository, issue, or pull request commands.
Use structured output when another tool or script must consume tea results.
anti_patterns: Do not run merge or close commands without confirming the target ID and user intent.
Do not assume GitHub or GitLab commands work against a Gitea remote.
Do not parse human-formatted command output when tea can return JSON or YAML.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps users work with Gitea repositories through the tea command line interface.

faq.question: Does it install tea automatically?
faq.answer: No. The user must install and configure the tea CLI before using these commands.

faq.question: How does it detect Gitea?
faq.answer: It suggests checking git remote values and treating non GitHub or GitLab remotes as possible Gitea instances.

faq.question: Can it create pull requests?
faq.answer: It provides the tea command pattern for creating pull requests after checking repository state.

faq.question: Can it manage issues?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents tea commands to list, view, create, close, and comment on issues.

faq.question: Is it useful for automation?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends JSON or YAML output flags so command results can be consumed by other tools.
